links.targetTitle: The Frozen Period requires an Atlas Edit Proposal to sit unc

title: The weekly Atlas edit path demands twice the Yes vote-weight of the monthly path
content:
A.1.12.2.6 sets two independent conditions for a monthly Ratification Poll to succeed and edit the Atlas: "Yes vote-weight must exceed No vote-weight when the poll closes" **and** "Yes vote-weight must exceed the Minimum Positive Participation value of 240,000,000 SKY when the poll closes." The poll is a binary yes/no/abstain running for two weeks.

Compare A.1.11.2.4, which requires "at least 480,000,000 SKY equivalents of Yes votes" for an Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal decided by a three-day Poll.

The inversion is deliberate and worth stating plainly: the *cheaper, faster* route requires **double** the affirmative support. The monthly path can settle for half the Yes weight because it has already extracted assurance elsewhere — a week of Feedback Period, a week of Frozen Period, template verification, a Core Facilitator misalignment review at Formal Submission, and a fortnight of open voting. The weekly path compresses all of that into three days, so the only remaining filter is raw mobilized support.

The design principle is that scrutiny and turnout are substitutes for legitimacy. Sky lets proposers choose which currency to pay in — deliberation time or vote-weight — but not to skip both. The practical consequence is that the weekly cycle is reserved in effect for changes an unusually large bloc already agrees on, while contested or complex edits are pushed into the monthly pipeline where argument, not mobilization, does the work.
description: Monthly Ratification Polls need 240,000,000 SKY of Yes weight over a two-week vote; weekly Atlas edits need 480,000,000 over three days — the faster route carries the higher bar.
